_README: LEDGER for the bookworm -> trixie migration of the emulator-bridge guest base.
The lab HOST is Debian 13 (trixie). The shared bridge guest base is still
Debian 12 (bookworm), and ~29 tiles overlay it read-only. A single flag-day
rebuild is not possible: each tile needs its own overlay rebuild, golden
re-bake and framebuffer acceptance, and several need real per-tile work
So the migration is GRADUAL and this file is its single source of truth.
Each bridge tile declares which suite its overlay is built on. Two bases
coexist; the bookworm one is frozen and is never touched again.
TO MIGRATE A TILE: do the per-tile work, rebuild its overlay against the
trixie base, bake the golden, verify with a real framebuffer screenshot,
and only THEN flip its entry here from "bookworm" to "trixie" in the same
commit. Flipping this file alone changes nothing on the box -- it declares
intent, and scripts/dev/bridge-suite-status.sh fails loudly when the
Consumed by scripts/build-guests/lib/bridge-suite.sh. Not generated: never
run stations-registry.py against it, and do not move it into registry/stations/.

bookworm._note: FROZEN 2026-07-15. 13 live overlays back onto this byte-for-byte (28 before the migration began). Never rebuild it: `bridge-base.sh --suite bookworm` refuses without --i-know-this-breaks-every-overlay. Count the `tiles` map below rather than trusting this sentence; `scripts/dev/bridge-suite-status.sh` is the authority.

trixie._note: BUILT 2026-08-10, runtime-proven (generic kernel + e1000 + bochs-drm + bare-X kiosk + hatari/EmuTOS on a sandbox clone). Matches the host suite, so a host-built binary runs in the guest unchanged and the per-tile ABI chroots stop being necessary. Wave 1 landed atarist/pdp11/gt40 and later decos; wave 2 the MAME tiles bbcmicro/armeval/zx81/dragon32/oricatmos; wave 4 the six VICE tiles c128/vic20/plus4/pet2001/cbm8032/cbm2 -- all 2026-08-10. It now carries live overlays and is frozen IN FACT: the flag below stays false, but bridge-base.sh treats a suite as frozen if the flag is set OR if any tile is declared on it, so the guard armed itself the moment the first tile migrated. Do not hand-flip it.

_notes.nextstep: 2026-08-20 rerun (rolled back by the driver): every trixie step passed, including media staging — attempt 1's curl SSL flake did not recur — and the pinned SDL3 3.4.14 source build was kept as-is. The builder died at first light: with no previous.cfg on the fresh overlay, Previous showed its Main menu and, after the builder's Enters, the ROM dialog 'NeXT Computer: ROM file not found!' (default Rev_1.0_v41.BIN); wait_for_workspace timed out at 600 seconds and the driver's automatic rollback restored the bookworm overlay (station active, frame byte-identical to the golden scene). Root cause: 085c074 (2026-08-11, tablet promotion) moved the previous.cfg write to after the first-light block, and no new-overlay build has run since the original builder (3fbdf86) wrote it before first light, so the regression stayed latent — the live bookworm tile's overlay still carries the original cfg, which is why the station never misbehaved. Nothing implicates trixie and the driver was sound; the fix (coordinator's call) is to restore the pre-first-light cfg write in scripts/build-guests/tiles/nextstep.sh. The owed SDL-init check is settled: the 'ERROR: Could not initialize the SDL library:' line is the builder's headless `previous --version 2>&1 | head -1 || true` probe (nextstep.sh:495) — SDL X11 init cannot succeed without a DISPLAY and the probe is structurally unable to fail, so it is weak but harmless; the real gates are the ns_ready pixel predicates and tile-accept.sh. The failed image is kept at overlay.qcow2.trixie-failed (now the attempt-2 overlay); evidence in /data/vms/sandbox/nextstep-trixie-rerun/evidence/attempt-2/. The station stays bookworm.
